Renee P: Noticing an odd binpack pattern in ap-southeast1 this morning. Aggregated GPU utilization across nodes is ~64% but pending tiny training jobs are stuck in Pending state with 'no nodes are available that match the requested resources'.
Diego M: That's the classic fragmentation case. We have a lot of 4-GPU nodes partially used by long-running inference replicas. Tiny jobs request 1-GPU with strict affinity, so scheduler can't pack them.
Ava T: Any recent changes to pod specs or node labels?
Renee P: Yes, runtime-team rolled out node label `gpu.class=highmem` to a subset of racks and some deployments were updated to require `nodeSelector: gpu.class: highmem` accidentally. That left many 1-2 GPU slots unusable for general training.
Diego M: Oof. We should tolerate that and either revert label requirement or broaden allowed node selectors. Quick mitigation: add admission webhook to rewrite nodeSelector for pending pods to prefer but not require `gpu.class`.
Ava T: Admission rewrite might be heavy. Short term: run a defrag job to evict low-priority inference replicas and move them to non-highmem nodes. We can use eviction API with maxUnavailable 30% on inference deployment.
Nikhil K: Cost/CAD note: evicting and moving these replicas will cause extra egress between racks while images pull. Should factor into cost for this maintenance window.
infra-bot: started defrag job job/defrag-20260315-01 (eta 12m).
Renee P: Also opened a ticket to runtime-team to fix the label rollout: runtime/9876. They need to make the label opt-in via toleration instead of nodeSelector.
Diego M: Long-term: implement a packing-aware scheduler predicate that considers node label flexibility and can reshuffle lower-priority pods to make room for small GPU requests. Also consider fractional GPU pool (1 GPU instances) in this region if demand for tiny jobs persists.
Ava T: Agree. For immediate visibility, adding a heatmap in console for "supplyable_gpus_by_request_size" would help product teams tune defaults.
Renee P: Action items: 1) Run defrag job (infra-bot) 2) Runtime team to revert nodeSelector 3) Diego to prototype soft-reserve + packer predicate 4) Nikhil to estimate maintenance egress cost and notify finance.
infra-bot: defrag job completed. Freed 28 1-GPU slots. ETA for full remediation depends on runtime-team patch.
Nikhil K: Shared cost estimate: ~USD 120 for egress + spot image pulls for the evicted replicas (approx). Logging this for chargeback.
Renee P: Thanks team. Monitoring pending queue now.
